selections.rationale: Explicit contract-clarification recovery of a repair task, not reference-fix: replacing the embedded complete known-bad source and its corresponding repair description is permitted to target exactly one current realistic defect, while retaining all original corrected objectives and public APIs. Keep the complete embedded source byte-identical to the derived known_bad_code; do not require the derived prompt to equal the immutable original prompt. Preserve aggregate_metrics API, exact event schema, validation of all events including rejected rows, accepted-only count/sum, first-accepted category order and fresh outputs. Clarify that finite exact integer/rational Real values are not converted to float for validation; bool is excluded and ordinary nonfinite floats are invalid. Totals start from integer zero and use native numeric addition in accepted-event order. Arbitrary-precision integer and standard Fraction totals remain exact; native mixed-operation OverflowError propagates without reclassification as malformed input, and finite float inputs may produce native infinity without an extra output-finiteness rule. No input mutation or partial returned result on failure. Embed complete faulty code with accepted-only predicate already corrected and only the realistic lossy finiteness-validation defect retained. Tests must include accepted 10**500, integer cancellation, Fraction controls, rejected huge values, later malformed rejected events, order/count and independent outputs. Do not narrow Mapping classes, cap integers, change global digit limits or invent custom-number exception behavior. Fresh r14 architecture retry only; retain the entire approved r11 contract scope above. Return exactly exp-v1-recovery-r14-python-repair-0138 as the structured output ID. The r11 output returned the original parent ID and failed the strict-ID guard; do not rename or reuse that rejected output. Produce fresh architecture artifacts for the normal independent-test pipeline; this is not an oracle critic correction.
